adopted: Use the open Agent Skills folder format with progressive disclosure.
Keep only the bootstrap router visible and search summaries before loading instructions.
Return no match when lexical evidence is weak instead of forcing a top result.
Bind reviewed skills to exact bundle SHA-256 digests and verify them again before resolving a path.
Use packet-scoped source IDs and compact generated indexes.
Keep future MCP transport compatible with resource discovery concepts without freezing an experimental draft.
findings: The ecosystem is converging on search-first progressive disclosure for collections above a few dozen skills.
Existing open-source loaders solve transport and installation, but reviewed admission, decision history, and fail-closed matching remain separate concerns.
Relative ranking alone can return an irrelevant best result for an unanswerable query.
Bundle integrity and security evaluation are increasingly treated as admission gates, not discovery features.
A plain local CLI is the smallest portable baseline; MCP and host adapters can remain external.
method: Ran seven fresh Exa searches, inspected primary repositories and specifications, pinned full revisions, compared discovery, loading, integrity, and evaluation behavior, and tested the failure assumptions against the proposed local design.
open_questions: When the MCP skills extension is stable enough to justify a separate adapter repository.
At what library size lexical search recall should be benchmarked against a hybrid retriever.
Whether signed review attestations are needed beyond local digest binding.
queries: open source agent skill index search load on demand context window
provider neutral Agent Skills repository MCP discovery
agent skill provenance SHA-256 bundle verification
agent skill security scanner evaluation open source
large agent skill library retrieval no match behavior
question: What portable architecture lets agents search hundreds of reviewed skills without bloating session context?
rejected: Loading every skill description into every coding session.
Making one provider's directory layout or UI metadata part of the repository contract.
Automatically loading the highest-ranked result when the match is weak.
Executing scripts from the index or treating discovery as action authority.
Forking a full external runtime into this repository.
skipped: A vector database in the first release because it adds dependencies before lexical recall is measured.
A hosted registry because the portable Git repository and generated JSON are sufficient for the first release.
Provider adapters because they create collision-prone maintained surfaces.
Signing and transparency logs until the threat model and distribution path require them.
